svg.title: Four Core Seats, Two Explicit Scale Additions
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-four-to-six-person-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Four Core Seats, Two Explicit Scale Additions; subtitle: Conservative and Base: 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled: 2 FT + 4 C.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: FT means full-time seat; C means contractor seat, not a full-time-equivalent assertion. Each numeric value represents one person. The first four seats form the baseline pod; the final two are scaled-only additions. Do not total all six seats as Base staffing or assume identical contractor hours.; caption: The founder remains accountable for pricing and delivery economics. Automation supports consent tracking, CRM routing, and lead-quality reporting; named people still own exceptions and client acceptance.; stages: label: Founder and commercial owner; value: Core seat: one full-time owner leads commercial decisions.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own positioning, sales, contracts, client relationships, contribution review, and unresolved delivery issues. At scale, delegate routine account operations to the added full-time client-success lead.; label: Data and CRM operator; value: Core seat: one contractor owns provenance and routing.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Maintain account deduplication, source records, consent evidence where required, suppression propagation, access permissions, and HubSpot or Salesforce assignment rules.; label: Outbound infrastructure operator; value: Core seat: one contractor owns authorized outreach operations.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Maintain domain authentication, mailbox configuration, provider-limit adherence, message scheduling, bounce review, and complaint investigation. Escalate delivery problems without bypassing provider restrictions.; label: Qualification and call-routing operator; value: Core seat: one contractor verifies conversations and handoffs.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review replies, qualify commercial need, confirm calendars, route calls, and collect acceptance evidence. Track no-shows and rejection causes without billing merely booked appointments.; label: Client-success lead; value: Scaled addition: one full-time employee owns account delivery.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Join only in the six-person configuration. Own client reporting, renewal preparation, delivery commitments, acceptance disputes, and capacity planning across active accounts.; label: Quality and reporting analyst; value: Scaled addition: one contractor owns independent quality review.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Join only in the six-person configuration. Audit qualification records, reconcile accepted units to invoices, analyze acquisition cost, and identify sources creating excessive replacement work.
